extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media scholars, students, and general readers interested in journalism movements
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the defining principles, practices, and values of the slow journalism movement — a journalism subculture that emphasizes time, depth, and social responsibility over speed and churn. Useful for practitioners and researchers seeking criteria that distinguish slow journalism from mainstream news production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core mindset: social responsibility over profit
rubrics_metrics.description: The core mindset of slow journalism is 'social responsibility of the outlet and less so on profit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle shapes editorial choices, prioritizing public-interest reporting and civic value rather than commercial imperatives. It implies decision-making that favors quality and societal benefit even when not immediately profitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content focus: long reports and in-depth investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Slow journalism 'tends to focus on long reports and in-depth investigations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize sustained reporting, deep research, and comprehensive coverage rather than short, rapidly produced items. Examples include long-form features and investigative projects that allocate time to develop sources and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working process: take time to find things out
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterized as storytelling that gives equal value to narrative craft and factual discovery, 'taking time to find things out, notice stories that others miss, and communicate it all to the highest standards.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial processes should allow slower timelines for reporting, verification, and narrative development. Measure success by depth, accuracy, and storytelling quality rather than speed of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about sourcing and origins
rubrics_metrics.description: Associated with a push for 'transparency, as it strives to be clear about how information is obtained by crediting all sources and clarifying what content is original and what is reproduced.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices include explicit source attribution, explaining reporting methods, and labeling reproduced or aggregated content. Transparency is a concrete criterion for trustworthiness and distinguishes original reporting from re-use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal value on narrative craft and factual discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Slow journalism values both narrative craft and factual discovery equally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should consider literary or narrative quality (structure, voice, engagement) alongside rigorous fact-gathering, verification, and evidence. Strong pieces harmonize storytelling techniques with journalistic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antidote to churnalism and advertorial content
rubrics_metrics.description: Positions itself against mainstream media that is described as 'filled to the brim with reprinted press releases, kneejerk punditry, advertorial nonsense and 'churnalism'.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid practices such as republishing press releases without reporting, prioritizing punditry over reporting, or publishing advertorial/PR content as journalism. Originality, independent reporting, and skepticism toward PR are evaluative criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific relationships with audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles can be distinguished by 'the specific relationships with its audience' that slow journalism outlets cultivate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes fostering engaged, possibly subscription- or membership-based communities, clearer communication about methods, and audience expectations of depth. Evaluate how an outlet involves, informs, and maintains accountability to its readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylistic alignment with long-form/literary/narrative journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Slow journalism 'shares similarities and has been associated with forms of journalism like long-form journalism, literary journalism, narrative journalism, and new journalism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of narrative techniques, literary prose, and extended contextualization are stylistic criteria. Pieces may be judged on how well they adapt literary modes while retaining factual rigor and journalistic ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual vagueness and contested definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers have noted that 'the concept is vague and not easily definable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that boundaries and definitions vary across outlets and contexts; avoid a rigid checklist. This is a meta-criterion: when evaluating whether something qualifies as 'slow journalism,' consider multiple dimensions (content, process, audience relations, values) rather than a single binary test.
